guides.name: Aisha K. Shahid
guides.bio:
Aisha K. Shahid founded All Neighborhoods Powerfully United in 2020, during the wave of organizing that followed the murder of George Floyd, beginning with a community gathering at Houston's SHAPE Center. In the years since, ANPU has run neighborhood cleanups, clothing and food drives, and direct support for people in crisis — including domestic violence rescue and helping people move into safer situations.

Her teaching comes out of the same commitment. She leads free and donation-based classes in public places so the practice stays within reach of anyone in Houston, whatever they can pay. Most Sunday mornings she teaches Empowerment Yoga at Emancipation Park in Third Ward.

Cadenza Arthouse has documented her work since 2020.

guides.name: Nahnah
guides.descriptor: Yoga instructor and holistic wellness guide
guides.bio:
Nahnah was born and raised in Houston, in South Park. She came to yoga in 2022, after leaving the military, looking for something with more depth than the content work she had been doing until then.

Her teaching is shaped by travel. She spent a month in Thailand at twenty-four — one week with her husband, the other three solo — and two weeks in Japan in December, where she took a local class and noticed what the studio did afterwards: everyone sat in a circle with tea and talked about their lives.

What she brings back is aimed squarely at home. She is direct about why: the neighborhood she grew up in did not have easy access to the things that keep people well, and she treats that as a problem worth solving rather than a fact of life. She teaches across Houston — parks, community gardens, rooftops, studios and the beach — on a schedule that changes month to month.
